docs.title: Cosmonautics
docs.text:
A survival space program for Paper

Build launch sites, fly player-built rockets, survive vacuum, assemble an orbital station, and establish a foothold on the Moon.

Install Cosmonautics Begin your journey

Beta.7 release scope: Earth, the Moon, stationary Stations, ordinary rockets, and Solo/Duo Lunar Rovers. Additional planets, moving Station voyages, and Station thrusters remain unreleased.

New in beta.7

Find Lunar Scrap in secured Moon colony loot rooms, refine it into Lunar Alloy at a powered Station, and build your Lunar Rover. Try /cosmo tutorial moon-workshop for the interactive lesson. This update also improves Station performance and tutorial interactions.

docs.title: What players can do
docs.text:
• Follow the Space Program advancement journey.
  • Build an Artemis launch site and fly directly between Earth and the Moon.
  • Manage suits, oxygen, pressure, habitats, and decompression hazards.
  • Practice zero-gravity movement, tethering, and station construction.
  • Explore lunar terrain and catacombs, then establish a breathable Moon base.
  • Refine Lunar Scrap and craft Hydrogen-powered Solo and Duo rovers.

docs.title: Build a space program
docs.text:
Follow advancements from early rocketry to orbital operations and a Moon landing and return.

See the Space Program

docs.title: Launch real missions
docs.text:
Build a pad, wire Mission Control, assemble Artemis, fuel it, and climb aboard.

Learn about rockets

docs.text:
Manage sealed suits, Oxygen Canisters, pressure, airlocks, habitats, and EVA movement.

Prepare for space

docs.text:
Land in a habitat-equipped lunar module, explore catacombs, and build a breathable base.

Explore the Moon

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Players should begin with the Player Guide and use /cosmo guide in game. Server owners should read Installation, then review Configuration and Permissions.

Early access

This wiki documents the supported beta journey. Coming-soon destinations remain clearly separated from playable release content.

docs.title: What Is Cosmonautics?
docs.text:
Cosmonautics turns a Paper survival server into a player-built space program. Progress begins with launch infrastructure on Earth, expands into orbital flight and optional Station operations, and leads to a complete expedition to the Moon.

The plugin is built around physical preparation. Players craft life-support equipment, construct launch sites, supply real building materials and propellant, board animated vehicles, and learn to survive environments where gravity and breathable air can no longer be taken for granted.

A completed Artemis vehicle and its surrounding launch infrastructure.

docs.title: The core journey
docs.text:
1. Reveal the Space Program advancement tab and establish Mission Control.
  2. Produce Rocket Fuel and Oxidizer while preparing the 10 × 10 launch site.
  3. Assemble and board an Artemis rocket.
  4. Equip a sealed suit and carry Oxygen Canisters.
  5. Fly directly to the Moon, or visit the optional orbital Station first.
  6. Explore lunar terrain and catacombs, then establish a breathable habitat.
  7. Fuel the lander's ascent stage and return to Earth.

docs.title: Designed for survival servers
docs.text:
Cosmonautics keeps its systems inside the Minecraft world. Pressure depends on sealed spaces. Station machinery depends on power. Rockets require preparation. Advancements explain the intended journey without locking commands, recipes, or travel behind the advancement screen.

Interactive tutorials demonstrate major systems with client-only blocks, entities, interfaces, and items. They never alter the real world or a player's inventory.

docs.title: Current release scope
docs.text:
Beta.7 supports Earth, the Moon, stationary Stations, ordinary rockets, and Solo/Duo Lunar Rovers. Stations are optional for the direct Earth–Moon journey and required for Lunar Alloy refining. Additional planets, moving Station voyages, Station thrusters, and the solar-system Dynmap view remain unavailable in release builds.

Begin the player journey View interactive tutorials

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: The main command is /cosmo.

docs.title: Player commands
docs.text: Command Purpose /cosmo guide Show the core progression guide. /cosmo status Show destination, suit, oxygen, canisters, and fuel. /cosmo planets Browse destinations and their release status. /cosmo route <destination> Show launch requirements and the next action. /cosmo launch <destination> Launch when route requirements are met. /cosmo return Show the correct return method for your location. /cosmo rocket Open the Earth rocket and launch-site guide. /cosmo tutorial Open the interactive tutorial catalog. /cosmo tutorial <tutorial-id> Start launch-site, survive-space, space-station, or moon-workshop. /cosmo tutorial stop Stop your current private tutorial. /cosmo station Open Station management, crew, and visitor controls.

docs.title: Administrator commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose /cosmo give [player] <item> [count] Give a custom Cosmonautics item; count must be from 1 to 1,000. /cosmo diagnostics Show operational diagnostics. /cosmo diagnostics report Write a sanitized local support report. /cosmo reload Reload supported plugin configuration. /cosmo reload rocketdesigns Reload rocket definitions.

Support reports are written under plugins/SpacePlugin/support-reports/ and exclude inventories, player data, and raw configuration contents.

See Interactive Tutorials for lesson contents and controls.

Station ship navigation and voyage commands belong to the unreleased interplanetary expansion and are unavailable in beta.7 release builds. Debug mode and operator permissions do not unlock them.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Cosmonautics generates plugins/SpacePlugin/config.yml. Stop Paper before editing it, or apply supported changes with /cosmo reload. Older configurations receive a timestamped backup before migration.

docs.title: Worlds and ownership
docs.text:
Each destination maps to a unique world name. Its world-modes value determines ownership:

  • generated: Cosmonautics owns the generator and settings.
  • existing: another provider owns and loads the world; Cosmonautics will not create, delete, or replace it.

Protect imported worlds

Never mark an irreplaceable imported world as generated. Back up the server before changing world ownership.

docs.title: Gameplay settings
docs.text:
The main configuration groups cover:

  • Gravity and zero-gravity RCS movement
  • Oxygen reserves, breathing, and vacuum damage
  • Sealed-room pressure, air quality, and decompression
  • Planetary environmental processing
  • Station power, processing, and personal docks
  • Rocket countdowns, structure consumption, and fuel costs
  • Crafting recipe availability

Invalid bounded numeric values are clamped and reported during startup. Duplicate or unsafe world names are refused when they could endanger world data.

docs.title: Production safety
docs.text: Keep debug.enabled: false on production servers. It exposes support/developer tools and is not needed for normal gameplay. Release builds independently disable additional planets, moving Station voyages, Station thrusters, and solar-system Dynmap; configuration, debug mode, and administrator permissions cannot enable them.

docs.title: License activation
docs.text:
Licensing is not configured in config.yml. Use the personalized JAR from your marketplace account. It activates online through RIC on first use. If support supplies a manual key, put it alone in plugins/SpacePlugin/license.key; this takes precedence over the embedded marketplace activation.

RIC authentication is required at startup. Later starts can validate a current cached signed lease or activate online when needed. Mid-session renewal and six-hour expiry shutdown are disabled by default after startup succeeds; the next startup checks licensing again. Preserve the plugin-managed licensing state when backing up or moving the installation.

docs.title: Lunar progression and external worlds
docs.text: The Lunar Alloy process needs a powered Station brewing stand and Lunar Scrap from secured colony loot rooms. An external Moon retains its provider's terrain and structures, so adopting it does not generate Cosmonautics catacombs or create a Scrap supply. The server owner must provide suitable loot or another source if the provider does not supply it.

docs.title: Rovers
docs.text: Beta.7 adds no rover-specific configuration settings. One Hydrogen bottle provides up to ten minutes of powered driving at normal server speed, and a full tank holds four bottles. Parked rovers use no fuel. Preserve rovers.dat with the rest of the plugin data. See Lunar Rovers for recipes and controls.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• 64-bit Java 25
  • Paper 26.2 experimental build 71
  • PacketEvents 2.13.0 installed as a separate server plugin
  • A personalized Cosmonautics marketplace download, a valid license, and outbound HTTPS access to the RIC licensing service

Cosmonautics does not support Spigot, Folia, Purpur, Bedrock servers, proxies used as game servers, or older Minecraft versions. Compatibility with other Paper builds is not promised.

docs.title: Fresh installation
docs.text:
1. Stop Paper completely and back up the whole server directory.
  2. Download your personalized JAR from the marketplace where you purchased Cosmonautics. For MCModels beta.7, use SpacePlugin-0.1.0-beta.7-mcmodels.jar from your account's library.
  3. Place PacketEvents 2.13.0 and that Cosmonautics JAR in plugins/.
  4. Allow outbound HTTPS to the RIC licensing service, then start Paper. The personalized download activates online on first use and generates plugins/SpacePlugin/config.yml. If support provides a manual key, put it alone in plugins/SpacePlugin/license.key; that file takes precedence. Licensing is not a config.yml setting.
  5. Confirm the console reports a valid license and that SpacePlugin enabled for Paper 26.2.
  6. Run /cosmo diagnostics as an operator.

The required datapack, structures, loot tables, recipes, and Artemis rocket definition are bundled in the plugin. WorldEdit and a separate resource pack are not required.

RIC authentication is required at startup. After the initial online activation, later starts can validate a current cached signed lease or activate online when needed. Mid-session renewal and six-hour expiry shutdown are disabled by default after startup succeeds. Licensing is checked again at the next startup.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Stop Paper and back up every world plus plugins/SpacePlugin/ before replacing the JAR. Configuration migration creates a timestamped backup and adds missing defaults without overwriting configured values. Updates never regenerate or delete a world automatically.

Keep the complete plugin data folder, including licensing state and rovers.dat, which stores rover identities, ownership, fuel, and deployment state.

docs.title: Upgrading to beta.7
docs.text:
• Secured Moon colony loot-room chests now provide Lunar Scrap when their contents are first generated. Existing chests whose contents have not yet generated are eligible; already-generated contents are not refilled. No world regeneration is needed.
  • Refine Scrap at a powered Station brewing stand, then craft Lunar Alloy. Existing finished Alloy remains usable in equipment recipes.
  • Use /cosmo tutorial moon-workshop for the new lesson covering alloy, rovers, and weapons.
  • Release builds keep additional planets, moving Station voyages, Station thrusters, and solar-system Dynmap unavailable. Debug mode cannot enable the expansion. When replacing a development build, saved expansion records remain stored but inactive.

The known high-ascent rocket visibility issue remains unresolved in beta.7.

Do not downgrade worlds

Paper 26.2 world data cannot safely be downgraded. Restore the matching complete server backup if an older Paper or Cosmonautics version must be recovered.

docs.title: Removing Cosmonautics
docs.text: Stop Paper normally before removing the JAR. Keep plugins/SpacePlugin/ if you may reinstall the plugin; delete it only after making a backup.

docs.title: Exploring The Moon
docs.text:
The Moon is the destination at the heart of the current Cosmonautics release. Artemis delivers each pilot to a persistent landing site with a habitat-equipped lander and a fueled route home.

Earth hangs above the Moon's generated terrain.

docs.title: First landing
docs.text:
Completing an Artemis touchdown earns One Small Step and awards a Habitat Deployer. The lander's lower structure remains at the site while its ascent stage is reserved for the return journey.

The Moon has reduced gravity and no naturally breathable atmosphere. Keep your suit sealed and monitor oxygen whenever you leave protected air.

docs.title: Build a lunar home
docs.text:
Deploy a habitat, seal its structure, and establish breathable air. Continue building and use a Pressure Gauge to check your rooms before treating them as safe living space.

A finished lunar base uses sealed construction and greenery to maintain fully breathable air.

docs.title: Explore beneath the surface
docs.text:
Generated Cosmonautics Moon worlds include catacombs with authored rooms and loot. Enter prepared: surface life support remains necessary underground, and the route back to the lander still matters.

Look for secured colony loot rooms inside the generated catacombs. Their special loot chests provide Lunar Scrap, the starting material for Lunar Alloy. Finished Alloy is made at a Station, rather than collected directly from these chests.

A generated catacomb entrance exposed at the lunar surface.

Existing chests after the beta.7 update

The Scrap loot applies when a chest's contents are first generated, including eligible existing chests whose contents have not yet generated. Already-generated contents are not refilled. No world reset is needed.

docs.title: Make Lunar Alloy
docs.text:
Start the private lesson with /cosmo tutorial moon-workshop, or follow the process below.

Your first alloy needs Station access

A Station is optional for direct Earth–Moon travel, but required to refine Lunar Scrap. Bring a normal brewing stand, ice, glass bottles, and iron, and provide station power. The stand's vanilla recipe needs a blaze rod. Neither the stand, solar panels, nor asteroid collector requires Lunar Alloy; rovers and weapons are not prerequisites.

docs.title: 1. Produce Hydrogen
docs.text:
At a powered Station brewing stand, put one Ice in the top ingredient slot and one empty glass bottle in each of the three bottom slots. A full-power batch takes about 20 seconds and produces two Hydrogen bottles and one Oxygen bottle.

Run two batches to have enough Hydrogen for one Scrap. You can bring Ice from Earth or use the Station's existing Blue Ice → Packed Ice → Ice processing.

docs.title: 2. Brew Lunar Alloy Solution
docs.text:
Remove the gas outputs, then place:

Slot Ingredient Top ingredient slot 1 Lunar Scrap Each of the three bottom slots 1 Hydrogen bottle

Place the Scrap directly into the ingredient slot; vanilla shift-clicking does not route this head item there. Keep the protected battery slot clear of fuel or other items. At full power, the stand consumes the Scrap and turns all three Hydrogen bottles into three gray Lunar Alloy Solution bottles in about 20 seconds.

Use Hydrogen in every bottom slot: Oxygen, water, and empty bottles cannot substitute for it. Missing ingredients or unavailable power prevent the batch from completing.

Your browser does not support embedded video. You can download the Lunar Alloy brewing demonstration instead.

Lunar Scrap and three Hydrogen bottles brewing into Lunar Alloy Solution in the powered Electric Brewing Stand.

docs.title: 3. Craft finished Alloy
docs.text:
In your personal 2×2 crafting grid or a crafting table, place two Lunar Alloy Solution bottles and two iron ingots in four separate cells, in any order.

Shapeless: two Solution bottles and two iron ingots make one Lunar Alloy, in any arrangement.

In-game crafting example

The shapeless recipe produces one Lunar Alloy and returns two empty glass bottles. Shift-click crafting also returns the bottles; any returned bottles that cannot fit in your inventory drop at your feet. Use a player crafting grid: automated Crafter blocks do not support this recipe and do not consume its ingredients.

For a complete first run, bring 1 Scrap, 2 Ice, 6 empty glass bottles, and 2 iron ingots. After making one Alloy, you will also have 1 Solution, 1 Hydrogen, 2 Oxygen, and 2 empty bottles left.

Finished Alloy is used by the existing rover and equipment recipes. Scrap and Solution cannot substitute for it.

Drinking Solution

Lunar Alloy Solution is a crafting ingredient, but it can be drunk. It causes Nausea I for eight seconds, returns an empty glass bottle, and has no other special effects.

docs.title: Rovers and equipment
docs.text:
Use your Alloy to craft a Solo or Duo Lunar Rover. Both run on Hydrogen and can be placed on Earth or the Moon. Solo seats its owner; Duo adds a passenger seat.

The Moon workshop also previews these equipment recipes. All three are shapeless: use one item per occupied slot, in any arrangement.

Copper GunRocket LauncherHoming Rocket Ammo

Makes 1 Copper Gun: 1 copper horse armor + 1 spyglass + 1 crossbow + 1 Lunar Alloy.

Makes 1 Rocket Launcher: 1 iron horse armor + 1 observer + 1 crossbow + 1 Lunar Alloy.

Makes 4 Homing Rocket Ammo: 1 Rocket Fuel + 1 Oxidizer + 1 iron ingot.

These portable weapons work away from Earth. Right-click the Copper Gun to fire one copper nugget. With the Rocket Launcher, hold right-click to acquire a target, then release after lock; each shot consumes Homing Rocket Ammo. Follow the in-game prompts and your server's combat rules.

Thruster Assembly is reserved for the unreleased interplanetary expansion and is not part of this equipment progression.

docs.title: Return to Earth
docs.text:
Bring Rocket Fuel to the lectern inside the lander habitat. The lectern controls the remaining ascent stage and launches it directly home. Use /cosmo return if you need a reminder at the landing site.

External Moon worlds

A server can adopt a provider-owned Moon with a biome-only environment overlay. Its terrain and structures remain owned by that provider, so Cosmonautics catacombs are unavailable unless the provider supplies them. Such a world has no automatic source of colony Lunar Scrap unless the server owner provides suitable loot or another way to obtain it.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Cosmonautics keeps ordinary player commands broadly available while separating administrative and development capabilities.

Permission Default Purpose spaceplugin.tutorial Everyone View private client-side tutorials. spaceplugin.soyuz.launch Everyone Board and launch Soyuz passenger transports. spaceplugin.sputnik.launch Everyone Target and launch Sputnik reconnaissance rockets. spaceplugin.admin Operators Reload, diagnostics, and protected administration. spaceplugin.station.admin Operators Station archive administration; included by spaceplugin.admin. spaceplugin.give Operators Give custom Cosmonautics items. spaceplugin.ballistic.launch Operators Target and launch ballistic rockets.

Production servers

Keep debug.enabled off in production. Administrator permissions and debug mode cannot unlock additional planets, Station voyages, Station thrusters, or solar-system Dynmap in a release build.

docs.title: Your space program
docs.text:
Craft or launch a Firework Rocket to reveal the Space Program advancement tab. Its milestones guide development from Mission Control and propellant production through rockets, Station operations, and a Moon landing and return.

Advancements guide and reward supported actions; they do not lock recipes, commands, travel, or other features.

docs.title: Journey to the Moon
docs.text:
1. Craft a Launch Controller, Rocket Fuel, and Oxidizer.
  2. Run /cosmo tutorial launch-site to learn the private 10×10 Artemis construction lesson.
  3. Run /cosmo tutorial survive-space to learn suit equipment, pressure safety, and airlock operation.
  4. Build and board an Artemis launch site, or take the optional Station branch first.
  5. On the Moon, explore generated catacombs, create a breathable habitat, and find Lunar Scrap in secured colony loot rooms.
  6. Use the lectern inside the lander habitat with Rocket Fuel to launch the ascent stage home with your Scrap.
  7. Visit a Station and use its powered brewing stand to refine the Scrap into Solution, then craft Lunar Alloy for rovers and equipment. /cosmo tutorial moon-workshop demonstrates the process.

Safe tutorial boundary

Tutorials are private client-side lessons. They do not change real blocks, entities, inventories, player state, or gameplay state.

docs.title: Station and EVA
docs.text:
The Station is optional for direct Earth–Moon travel, but required for the Lunar Alloy production chain. In zero gravity, use movement input for RCS corrections and hold Shift for a forward burst. An EVA harness can tether you to nearby solid surfaces.

At the Station you can assemble modules, process asteroids, produce gases, refine alloy, and visit another player's dock. Moving Station voyages and thrusters remain unreleased.

Run /cosmo tutorial space-station for a private guided demonstration, then read the Orbital Station guide for a concise reference.

docs.title: When a launch is blocked
docs.text: Use /cosmo route <destination> to see the missing requirement and next action. /cosmo status summarizes your current destination, suit, oxygen, canisters, and fuel. /cosmo planets shows environmental information and release availability.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: Cosmonautics is in early access. This page separates playable release content from destinations retained for future development.

docs.title: Available now
docs.text:
• Earth-based progression, Mission Control, propellants, and launch-site construction
  • Direct Artemis travel between Earth and the Moon
  • Lunar pressure, oxygen, habitats, catacombs, resources, and settlement
  • Station construction, EVA, docking, asteroid processing, and gas production
  • Lunar Scrap → Lunar Alloy Solution → Lunar Alloy production
  • Player-owned Solo and Duo Lunar Rovers with Hydrogen fuel
  • Interactive Launch Site, Survive in Space, Space Station, and Moon workshop tutorials
  • The Space Program advancement journey

docs.title: Coming soon
docs.text:
The interplanetary expansion is unreleased. Its destinations and travel systems are unavailable in beta.7 release builds:

  • Mars
  • Europa
  • Asteroid Belt
  • Vulcanus
  • Moving Station voyages, including Earth–Moon Station travel
  • Station thrusters and Thruster Assembly
  • The solar-system Dynmap view

Their designs and availability may change while development continues. Configuration, debug mode, operator permissions, and commands cannot unlock this content in a release build.

docs.title: Documentation roadmap
docs.text:
Future wiki updates can add focused guides and screenshots without changing the top-level structure:

  • Illustrated Artemis construction and launch guide
  • Suit, oxygen, and habitat reference
  • Station building and EVA guide
  • Lunar exploration and resources guide
  • Administrator upgrade and external-world guides

docs.title: Rockets And Launch Sites
docs.text:
Rockets in Cosmonautics begin as infrastructure and materials, not a menu shortcut. The main Earth–Moon mission uses a player-built Artemis launch site with Mission Control, staged construction, propellant, and an animated flight.

Artemis on its completed pad, with the Launch Controller and supply infrastructure at its base.

docs.title: Build the launch site
docs.text:
The Artemis pad is a 10 × 10 structure. A complete site connects three important fixtures:

  • Launch Controller: the lectern used to inspect and operate the site.
  • Supply chest: holds construction materials, Rocket Fuel, and Oxidizer.
  • Comparator: points away from the controller and reports construction progress; signal 15 means the site is ready.

Run /cosmo tutorial launch-site for a private animated lesson showing the exact pad, controller wiring, chest placement, comparator direction, and Artemis assembly sequence.

docs.title: Construct and fuel Artemis
docs.text:
Open the Launch Controller to inspect missing structure materials and site status. Supplied materials are consumed as the vehicle assembles from its production parts. Rocket Fuel and Oxidizer then prepare the completed rocket for launch.

If launch is blocked, use /cosmo route <destination> for the missing requirement and next action. /cosmo rocket opens the launch-site guide.

docs.title: Flight and staging
docs.text:
Once ready, the mission includes ignition, powered ascent, stage separation, and the handoff to its destination. Detached mission stages can leave recoverable salvage after flight.

The wider Space Program also introduces V-2 development, Sputnik reconnaissance, and Soyuz passenger transport. Artemis remains the supported direct route between Earth and the Moon.

Known beta.7 visual issue

A rocket can become invisible late in ascent, around 1,700–2,000 blocks high. This visual issue remains unresolved in beta.7.

docs.title: Returning from the Moon
docs.text:
The lunar lander remains at its assigned landing site. Place Rocket Fuel into the lectern inside its habitat and use that control to launch the ascent stage home. /cosmo return explains the correct return method for your current destination.

Prepare before launch

Wear a complete sealed suit and carry Oxygen Canisters before leaving Earth. Space and the Moon cannot be treated like breathable overworld environments.

docs.title: Lunar Rovers
docs.text:
Lunar Rovers are player-owned, Hydrogen-powered vehicles for Earth and the Moon. Craft a Solo for one driver or a Duo to bring a passenger. Both use the same fuel and driving controls.

Start /cosmo tutorial moon-workshop to preview both recipes, placement, refuelling, and driving with floating W/A/S/D prompts.

Your browser does not support embedded video. You can download the Lunar Rover demonstration instead.

Place, fuel, and drive a Lunar Rover across the Moon's terrain.

docs.title: Choose and craft a rover
docs.text:
Both recipes need finished Lunar Alloy. Scrap and Solution do not work in its place.

Variant Seats Materials for one rover Solo Owner/driver 2 copper ingots, 1 saddle, 2 iron ingots, 1 Lunar Alloy, 2 blackstone Duo Owner/driver + 1 guest passenger 1 copper ingot, 2 saddles, 2 iron ingots, 1 Lunar Alloy, 2 blackstone

Use a crafting table and match the arrangement for your chosen variant. Each occupied slot holds one item.

docs.title: Duo — driver and passenger
docs.text: One Small Step reveals both recipes in the recipe book. The advancement is not required to craft them when you already have the materials.

docs.title: Place and fuel
docs.text:
1. Hold the rover in your main hand on Earth or the Moon.
  2. Right-click the top of solid ground, with clear space around the vehicle and no players or creatures inside its footprint.
  3. Newly crafted rovers start with an empty tank. Hold a Hydrogen bottle in your main hand and sneak-right-click the deployed rover to refuel.
  4. Right-click the rover normally to board. Only its owner drives; another player can right-click a Duo to take its passenger seat.

Hydrogen comes from a powered Station brewing stand. One bottle supplies about ten minutes of powered driving at normal server speed. A full tank holds four bottles, for about forty minutes. Parked rovers do not burn fuel.

Only a complete bottle's worth of fuel can be added at once. In Survival, refuelling returns an empty bottle; keep space for it when holding a stack of Hydrogen. If the tank is too full or there is no room for the returned bottle, refuelling is refused without consuming the Hydrogen.

docs.title: Drive
docs.text:
Default key Action W Drive forward S Reverse A / D Steer left / right Space Brake Shift Dismount

Steer with A/D; looking around with the mouse does not turn the rover. Your normal life-support equipment is still needed in vacuum.

docs.title: Pack and move
docs.text:
The owner can sneak-left-click a stopped, settled rover after everyone has dismounted. Keep a free inventory slot for the packed item. Packing retains the remaining fuel, so you can place it again without starting with an empty tank.

The Solo has no guest seat. Only the owner can refuel or pack either variant.

docs.title: The Space Program
docs.text:
The Space Program is an advancement journey through rocketry, survival equipment, orbital operations, and a Moon landing and return.

Craft or launch a Firework Rocket to reveal the tab. Progress begins after Cosmonautics is installed; earlier accomplishments are not inferred.

docs.title: Early rocketry
docs.text:
The opening milestones lead from lighting a Firework Rocket to building a launch pad and establishing Mission Control. Rocket Fuel and Oxidizer form parallel preparation branches before experimental V-2 and Sputnik development.

Fuel and Oxidizer milestones each track 30 crafted items. These advancements describe and reward the journey; they do not lock the underlying recipes or commands.

docs.title: Orbital branch
docs.text:
The optional Station branch includes:

  • Low Earth Orbit: arrive at a Station by a normal rocket mission.
  • Station Online: bring a Station machine online with adequate solar power.
  • Harvest the Heavens: be present when a powered asteroid collector delivers resources.
  • Orbital Defense: destroy an asteroid with the Station's Copper Cannon or Missile Turret.

Reaching low Earth orbit awards an EVA Harness.

docs.title: Moon branch
docs.text:
The lunar branch begins with Cleared for Launch, earned by boarding a complete, valid Artemis site, and One Small Step, earned by completing the Moon landing. It then branches to The Long Way Home, for completing the lander's return to Earth, and Home Away from Home, for successfully deploying a habitat in an oxygen-controlled world.

One Small Step awards a Habitat Deployer. The Long Way Home awards eight Firework Rockets. Other milestones award experience and occasional one-time items.

Continue beyond the advancement goals by exploring catacombs, refining Lunar Alloy, building a breathable base, and crafting Lunar Rovers. These activities do not require a separate advancement unlock.

docs.title: Guidance, not gates
docs.text: Advancements show useful goals and celebrate accomplishments, but they never gate commands, recipes, travel, or other plugin features. Use /cosmo guide for the concise in-game route and /cosmo route <destination> when you are unsure what a launch still requires.

docs.title: Orbital Station
docs.text:
The orbital Station supports construction, processing, EVA, and cooperative play. You can travel directly between Earth and the Moon without completing Station content, but Station access is required to produce Hydrogen and refine Lunar Scrap into Alloy for rovers and equipment.

Station EVA with solar power, the planet display, and a visible harness tether.

Start with the interactive lesson:

/cosmo tutorial space-station

docs.title: Founding and arrival
docs.text:
A founding rocket carries the first station into orbit with its construction cargo. A station begins with a canonical shell, a docking route, and clear-sky blue solar panels. Passenger capsules approach in stages before docking with the station.

Use /cosmo station to open Station management, crew, and visitor controls. Released Stations remain in their supported orbit. Station voyages, including moving a Station between Earth and the Moon, and Station thrusters belong to the unreleased interplanetary expansion. Ordinary rocket travel and Station docking remain available.

docs.title: Power and processing
docs.text:
Station machines share the Station's solar-panel supply. Other active machines increase total demand. The tutorial demonstrates the number of panels required as each machine is introduced.

  • Break suitable asteroids manually to recover materials.
  • Process Blue Ice through the Electric Furnace into Packed Ice and Ice.
  • Use the Electric Brewing Stand to turn Ice and empty bottles into Hydrogen and Oxygen.
  • Build an Asteroid Collector Controller above its Observer to automate collection.
  • Collectors extend an articulated arm, retrieve a target fragment, and eject recovered resources behind the controller.

docs.title: Hydrogen and Oxygen
docs.text:
Use a normal brewing stand recognized by the Station, with sufficient clear-sky blue solar panels connected to the Station's shared power supply. With default settings, four panels fully power one brewer when no other machines are drawing power. The battery shown in its fuel slot is a protected power display; leave the physical fuel slot empty, and do not insert or try to take a battery item.

Put 1 Ice in the top ingredient slot and 1 empty glass bottle in each of the three bottom slots. After about 20 seconds at full power, the batch produces 2 Hydrogen bottles + 1 Oxygen bottle. Reduced Station power slows processing, and insufficient power pauses progress.

Hydrogen fuels Lunar Rovers and is an ingredient in Lunar Alloy refining. The same powered stand combines 1 Lunar Scrap + 3 Hydrogen bottles → 3 Lunar Alloy Solution bottles. Put Scrap in the top slot and Hydrogen in all three bottom slots. Ordinary potion brewing remains available; follow each recipe's inputs.

docs.title: Defense machines
docs.text: The guided lesson demonstrates the Station's Copper Cannon and Missile Turret after the core processing systems. Treat these as operator-controlled station equipment and follow their in-game prompts for valid use.

docs.title: Access and return
docs.text: The Station Controller previews ownership and visitor access settings. When you are ready to leave, board the docked passenger capsule for the Earth-return sequence.

docs.title: EVA safety
docs.text:
Station space is zero gravity. Use movement input for RCS corrections and hold Shift for a forward burst. An EVA Harness can tether you to a nearby solid surface.

Prepare before going outside

Wear a complete sealed suit and carry Oxygen Canisters before entering vacuum. Use /cosmo status to check your equipment and oxygen state.

docs.title: Surviving Space
docs.text:
Space is hostile even when the rocket works perfectly. Cosmonautics models breathable air, oxygen reserves, pressure loss, decompression, low- and zero-gravity movement, and the equipment needed to survive them.

The Pressure Gauge confirms that this sealed Moon base is pressurized with 100% breathable air.

docs.title: Your survival equipment
docs.text:
• Glass helmet and white suit: a complete sealed outfit for vacuum exposure.
  • Oxygen Canisters: carried reserves for places without breathable air.
  • Pressure Gauge: checks whether the surrounding atmosphere is safe.
  • EVA Harness: creates a visible safety tether to a nearby solid surface.
  • Magnetic Boots: station equipment for controlled movement around metal structures.

Use /cosmo status to review your suit, oxygen, canisters, fuel, and current destination.

docs.title: Pressure and breathable rooms
docs.text:
A room must be sealed before it can hold pressure. Even one broken block can vent its atmosphere and trigger decompression. After resealing a pressurized room, greenery can improve its air until it becomes breathable.

Check with a Pressure Gauge before removing your helmet. The /cosmo tutorial survive-space lesson lets you breach and reseal a private demonstration room without changing real blocks.

docs.title: Airlocks
docs.text: Never open both airlock doors at once. Enter through the first door, close it behind you, then open the second door only after the chamber is isolated from the habitat.

docs.title: EVA and zero gravity
docs.text:
At the orbital Station, movement input provides RCS corrections and Shift gives a forward burst. Recoil and collisions matter when there is no ordinary gravity to bring you back down. Attach an EVA Harness near a solid surface before drifting away from the structure.

Vacuum checklist

Complete suit, Oxygen Canisters, known pressure state, and a safe return route should all be confirmed before leaving a pressurized area.

docs.title: Interactive Tutorials
docs.text:
Cosmonautics tutorials teach complete systems through private, interactive scenes. Open the catalog with:

/cosmo tutorial

Select a lesson in chat or start one directly with /cosmo tutorial <tutorial-id>. Use /cosmo tutorial stop to leave at any time.

The lessons, including Moon workshop, do not require an advancement unlock. The spaceplugin.tutorial permission is enabled for players by default.

docs.title: See a tutorial in action
docs.text:
Your browser does not support embedded video. You can download the Launch Site tutorial recording instead.

A short playthrough of the Launch Site lesson, from constructing the pad to previewing Artemis and its propellants.

docs.title: Launch Site
docs.text:
/cosmo tutorial launch-site

Build the 10 × 10 Artemis pad, craft and place the Launch Controller, connect its supply chest and progress comparator, preview Artemis assembly, and learn how Rocket Fuel and Oxidizer prepare the vehicle for launch.

Glowing objects and in-world prompts lead the player through each interactive step.

docs.title: Survive in Space
docs.text:
/cosmo tutorial survive-space

View recipes for a sealed suit, Oxygen Canisters, and the EVA Harness. The lesson then demonstrates pressure loss through broken glass, resealing and oxygenating a habitat, reading a Pressure Gauge, and cycling an airlock without opening both doors together.

Tutorial recipe windows are safe previews: click the output or close the window to continue.

docs.title: Space Station
docs.text:
/cosmo tutorial space-station

Follow a station-founding mission into orbit, dock with the new station, install solar panels, process ice and mineral asteroids, operate the automated collector and defensive machines, preview access settings, and return to Earth.

The Station lesson uses glowing targets to demonstrate asteroid processing and machinery.

docs.title: Moon workshop
docs.text:
/cosmo tutorial moon-workshop

Learn the complete Scrap-to-equipment route through five chapters:

  1. Find Lunar Scrap in a secured colony loot-room chest.
  2. Produce Hydrogen in a powered Station brewing stand.
  3. Brew Lunar Alloy Solution and craft finished Lunar Alloy.
  4. View both Solo and Duo rover recipes, placement, refuelling, and driving. Floating W/A/S/D prompts show forward movement, reversing, and steering.
  5. Preview the Copper Gun, Rocket Launcher, their ammunition, and how their shots behave.

The lesson demonstrates the existing recipes without giving you real items or firing real weapons. Thruster Assembly and interplanetary travel are outside this released lesson. See Exploring the Moon and Lunar Rovers for the written recipes and controls.

docs.title: Controls and interactions
docs.text:
• Follow action-bar narration and click glowing scene objects when prompted.
  • Clicking a machine or crafting target opens its preview immediately. In brewing previews, click the ingredient or any of the three bottom bottles to advance; the protected battery slot does not advance the lesson.
  • The Moon hydrogen demonstration needs one processing click; it does not make you repeat the batch.
  • Use the chat controls to move between chapters, replay, or exit. Interaction boundaries advance directly to the next glowing target.
  • A completed scene remains visible until you use its glowing finish target.
  • Only one tutorial session runs for you at a time.

Private and safe

Tutorial blocks, entities, inventories, recipes, machines, and items exist only in your client-side lesson. Tutorials do not alter real blocks, entities, inventories, player state, or gameplay state.
